expectations.text: References the EDPB's draft Guidelines 03/2026 on web scraping in the context of generative AI, adopted July 2026 (consultation until October 30, 2026)
expectations.evidence: "EDPB Guidelines 03/2026 on web scraping for generative AI (adopted for consultation 7 July 2026, consultation open until 30 October 2026)"

expectations.text: States that consent is generally not viable as a lawful basis at scraping scale, making legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)) the realistic basis
expectations.evidence: "Consent is generally not viable at scale for scraping the open web... Legitimate interest is treated as the realistic lawful basis"

expectations.text: Explains that legitimate interest requires a strict three-part balancing test with concrete mitigations/safeguards (e.g., excluding sensitive sources, respecting robots/opt-out signals, data minimisation)
expectations.evidence: "full three-step LIA: legitimate interest → necessity → balancing" plus concrete mitigations: filter special-category/children's data, opt-out signals, DPIA, provenance diligence

expectations.text: States that controllers are expected to publish detailed public privacy notices about the scraping (Art. 14 transparency)
expectations.evidence: "Controllers are expected to publish detailed, specific public notices describing the scraping and training activity (transparency - Art. 13/14...)"

expectations.text: Mentions facilitating data subject rights including pre-collection opt-out mechanisms, and that the guidance covers first-party scraping, contracted scraping, and purchased broker datasets
expectations.evidence: "a pre-collection opt-out mechanism (e.g., robots.txt-style signals, do-not-train headers...)"; "Coverage extends beyond your own first-party scraping to contracted scraping... and purchased broker/aggregator datasets"
